title: One-sided limit
body: A one-sided limit is the value f(x) approaches as x approaches c from only the left (x→c⁻) or only the right (x→c⁺); if the left and right limits are not equal, the two-sided limit does not exist.
ced_evidence: LIM-1.C.1 "The concept of a limit includes one sided limits"; LIM-1.C.4 "if the limit from the left does not equal the limit from the right"; LIM-1.D.1 "One-sided limits can be determined analytically or graphically"

title: Definition of continuity at x = c
body: f(c)\text{ exists},\quad \lim_{x\to c} f(x)\text{ exists},\quad \lim_{x\to c} f(x)=f(c)
ced_evidence: LIM-2.A.2 "A function f is continuous at x = c provided that f(c) exists, lim f(x) exists, and lim f(x) = f(c)"

title: Types of discontinuities
body: The CED names three types of discontinuity: removable, jump, and discontinuities due to vertical asymptotes.

items.label: Removable discontinuity
items.meaning: The limit exists at the discontinuity, so the discontinuity can be removed by defining or redefining the function value there to equal the limit.

items.label: Jump discontinuity
items.meaning: The limit from the left does not equal the limit from the right, so the two-sided limit does not exist.

items.label: Discontinuity due to a vertical asymptote
items.meaning: The function is unbounded near the point (an infinite limit), so the limit does not exist as a real number.

ced_evidence: LIM-2.A.1 "Types of discontinuities include removable discontinuities, jump discontinuities, and discontinuities due to vertical asymptotes"

title: Limits at infinity and end behavior
body: A limit at infinity extends the limit concept to x increasing or decreasing without bound, and it describes the end behavior of a function.
caution: End behavior is a limit as the variable approaches infinity (e.g., t→∞), not a limit as it approaches 0; write the correct limit notation.
ced_evidence: LIM-2.D.3 "The concept of a limit can be extended to include limits at infinity"; LIM-2.D.4 "Limits at infinity describe end behavior"

title: Function types continuous on their domains
body: These function types are continuous at all points in their domains.

items.label: Polynomial
items.meaning: Continuous on all points in its domain.

items.label: Rational
items.meaning: Continuous on all points in its domain.

items.label: Power
items.meaning: Continuous on all points in its domain.

items.label: Exponential
items.meaning: Continuous on all points in its domain.

items.label: Logarithmic
items.meaning: Continuous on all points in its domain.

items.label: Trigonometric
items.meaning: Continuous on all points in its domain.

caution: Continuity is guaranteed only on the domain; for example, a rational function is not continuous where its denominator is zero.
ced_evidence: LIM-2.B.2 "Polynomial, rational, power, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions are continuous on all points in their domains"

title: Continuity of a piecewise function at a boundary
body: For a piecewise-defined function to be continuous at a boundary of its partition, the expression on one side, the expression on the other side, and the function's value at the boundary must all be equal.
ced_evidence: LIM-2.C.2 "the value of the expression defining the function on one side of the boundary must equal the value of the expression defining the other side of the boundary, as well as the value of the function at the boundary"
